ink-950.purpose: the stage's ground, the command line's well, the switch's knob when on, the ring between overlapping faces, and the console log.

ink-900.purpose: the rail, and the console's title bar and prompt row.

ink-850.purpose: what floats over the stage: popovers, dialogs, the toast, a seal's menu; the console's status strip and command palette.

ink-800.purpose: seals, PLAY while it kindles or is closed, fields, checkboxes, the switch's track when off, faces, a seal's tip, a control while its popover is open, a menu row on hover, the progress track, the scrollbar's thumb; the console's chosen palette row.

line.purpose: hairlines: the rail's edge, a popover's head and sections, file rows, the window controls' divider, the command line's ring, and closed PLAY's edge.

line-strong.purpose: the ring round everything that floats (tip, menu, popover, dialog, toast), the Game chip's ring, and kindling PLAY's edge.

outline.purpose: an outline button's ring, the ring of + and of a seal under the pointer, a checkbox's ring, the Game chip's ring on hover or while open.

field-line.purpose: a field's ring and the switch's track when off: 3.2:1 against the ink-800 fill and 3.4:1 or more against the grounds around it, so a field's edge meets the 3:1 non-text floor.

scrim.purpose: behind a dialog. Darker than the boards' 42% under Add a server on purpose: 42% over a lit PLAY would leave two embers in view.

scrim-light.purpose: behind a popover; the top bar stays above it.

text.purpose: the server's name, titles and primary text (17:1 on ink-950).

text-prose.purpose: running sentences: the host's notice, a task's lede, a dialog's description, the stage's notes and What to try (13:1).

text-2.purpose: the state line, field labels, a seal's letter, the Game chip's words, a job's words in the Game popover (11:1).

muted.purpose: meta lines, a popover's lines, "playing", hints, quiet words, icon buttons, the + seal, placeholders (7.6:1).

faint.purpose: the address, closed PLAY's word (4.7:1 on ink-800), the window controls, footnotes, an offline seal's bar, What to try's bullets; console timestamps and separators (5.4:1 on ink-950).

on-ember.purpose: white on ember: PLAY's word, an ember button's, the 焚, and selected text.

ember-600.purpose: lit PLAY's fill, under a 10% white sheen; the fill of the one primary action of a task, a popover section or a dialog (Continue, Create account, Sign in, Add, Use it, Repair, Verify, Remove); and the 焚 seal. Always with white text (4.9:1).

ember-hover.purpose: lit PLAY and an ember button under the pointer, a step brighter than ember-600. Never at rest.

ember-500.purpose: where the player is and how far along: the active seal's 1 px edge, + while Add a server is open, the account's ring while its popover is open, the 2 px focus ring, the caret, text selection, the Game popover's 4 px progress fill, the bright end of PLAY's kindle fill (at 85%), the running PLAY's edge (at 55%) and lit PLAY's glow (at 70%).

ember-300.purpose: the 1 px inner edge of lit PLAY (at 50%, 70% on hover) and of an ember button (at 45%, 65% on hover). Never a fill.

ember-glow.purpose: the soft glow beside the kindle's leading edge (at 55%). Never on chrome.

ember-tint.purpose: the active seal's ground, the account's ground, the player's own face, and the running PLAY's ground (at 60%).

gold-300.purpose: people and places to go: the host's name before their notice, friends' names and initials, the account's initials, "Signed in as lin_yue", links, and the console's player names and prompt; and a setting that's on (the switch's track, the checkbox's tick).

gold-100.purpose: the kindle's 2 px leading edge, and a link on hover.

vignette-warm.purpose: the stage's ground, from the lower left, while PLAY is lit or the game runs.

vignette-warm-mid.purpose: the stage's ground, from the lower left, while PLAY is lit or the game runs.

vignette-cool.purpose: the stage's ground while PLAY kindles, while the copy needs something, and behind a task.

vignette-cool-mid.purpose: the stage's ground while PLAY kindles, while the copy needs something, and behind a task.

ok.purpose: online, Game ready, Verified, the running PLAY's dot; a seal's bar, an 8 px dot or a check.

warn.purpose: maintenance (a seal's bar, the state line's dot); a file that needs repair or a missing folder (the Game chip's words, dot and 40% ring, a repair's reasons); console WARN.

danger.purpose: a changed key, a key not yet trusted or a server this launcher can't play on (a seal's bar); errors and an unreachable server, always as the circled exclamation and words; an invalid field's ring and its message; console ERROR.

info.purpose: the info mark before the model's notice.

display.purpose: the server's name on the stage, up to two lines, then clipped. Cinzel draws it in capitals.

headline.purpose: a task's title: "Welcome to Fenji", "Join Moonward", "Sign in to Moonward".

dialog-title.purpose: "Add a server", "Remove Moonward?", "A new key for Moonward", "Run it yourself".

seal.purpose: a server's initial in its seal.

title.purpose: a popover section's heading: "Swords of Legends Online", "Steam library", "Moonward", "Auto-update".

status.purpose: the state line in text-2; a task's lede in Prose at line-height 1.5.

body.purpose: sentences; the host's notice and a dialog's description at 1.55, in Prose, up to 560 px wide.

body-small.purpose: the stage's notes and What to try in Prose, a field's text, a checkbox's label, quiet words.

button-secondary.purpose: Outline buttons and gold links, sentence case.

secondary.purpose: the Game chip, a seal's tip, meta lines, a popover's lines, hints, field errors, the friends' row, the toast's line.

label.purpose: field labels, in text-2, 10 px above the field.

small.purpose: initials on the account and the faces. The floor: no readable text is smaller.

mono.purpose: the address in the top bar, paths, a repair's file names, the command in Run it yourself; mono fields at 13.5 px; and the whole host console (line-height 1.75; 14 px on the prompt). A path under the player's home folder shows it as `~` ("~/Games/SoLO"), for display only, so a screenshot carries no player's name; on Windows, where `~` means nothing to a player, paths show whole.

mark.purpose: 焚 in the rail's seal, at 20 px.

shadows.name: Popover
shadows.purpose: Game, Account and Settings, over the light scrim.

shadows.name: PLAY's light

shadows.name: The kindle's edge

shadows.name: Rings

focus.name: focus-ring

gradients.name: ground-warm

gradients.name: ground-cool
gradients.purpose: The stage's ground while PLAY kindles, while the copy needs something, and behind a task.

gradients.name: play-sheen

gradients.name: kindle-fill
gradients.purpose: PLAY's fill while it kindles, behind a 2 px gold-100 leading edge.

motion.name: ease-in-out

motion.name: hover
motion.purpose: Hovers, open states and a seal's menu.

motion.name: scrim

motion.name: pop

narrative.overview:
Fenji is named for 焚寂, the cursed sword, and its light now lives in the one button the player came to press. The chosen server fills the window: its name inscribed in Cinzel, one line of state, its host's notice, PLAY, and the friends already in the lobby. While the game's files verify or Proton prepares, ember fills PLAY from the left; when the copy is ready, PLAY is alight and the stage's ground warms from the lower left. Readiness is felt on PLAY before it is read.

Everything else is quiet ink: a near-black stage, an ink-900 rail of square server seals, hairlines, warm off-white text. Ember is rationed to one action in view, gold marks people and places to go, and the four status hues only ever travel with words. Game, Account and Settings open as compact popovers under their own controls and close again; a task the player must finish takes the stage or a centred dialog; an update waits in a corner. The finish is a modern game launcher's (HoYoPlay, Riot Client, Battle.net) in xianxia restraint: no tabs, no side column, no key art, no news. The Ember Sword's launcher parts (the blade, the header with its wordmark and tabs, the context column) are retired; their boards stay in `docs/design/launcher/boards/` as the v0.5 record.

These tokens are Fenji's single identity, approved by the owner on 2026-10-13 and kept through the launcher's redesign of 2026-10-16, for the launcher, the host console, the website and the docs. The fonts (Cinzel, Geist, Geist Mono, and Noto Serif SC subset to 焚寂) are SIL Open Font License and ship inside each product; the launcher's content security policy is `default-src 'self'`, so nothing loads from a font CDN. The redesign's boards (`docs/design/launcher/redesign/screens.html`) are what the build follows, under the rulings in its spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-16-launcher-redesign-design.md`); where the build departs from a board, this file records the build and says why.
keyCharacteristics: Ink ground in tonal steps with hairlines; a shadow only on what floats over the stage.
One ember action in view, at most; gold for people and links; status colours only beside words.
PLAY kindles: it is the progress indicator and the brand's light at once.
A 72 px rail of square ink seals, each over a 3 px state bar.
Cinzel for the server's name and titles, Geist for the interface, Geist Mono for addresses, paths and the console.
A fixed 1200 × 720 window: the rail, a 56 px top bar, and the stage.
Short, true words; never a request for Steam or Gameforge credentials.

rules.name: The One Ember Rule
rules.body: One ember-600 action in view, at most: PLAY when it's lit, otherwise the one primary action of a task, a popover section or a dialog. Ember-500 marks where the player is (the active seal, focus, the caret, a selection, an open account) and progress. Nothing else is ember: not icons, not headings, not links, not switches.

rules.name: The Gold Is People Rule
rules.body: Gold marks people and places to go, and a setting that's on. It never fills an action button.

rules.name: The Status Never Alone Rule
rules.body: A status colour always travels with words, and an error also carries the circled exclamation. In the rail, a seal's bar has its words in the seal's tip and its accessible name.

rules.name: The Plaque Rule
rules.body: Cinzel is only for the server's name, the titles of tasks, dialogs and popovers, and a seal's letter. PLAY, buttons, labels and lines are Geist; addresses, paths and commands are Geist Mono.

rules.name: The Tracked Caps Rule
rules.body: PLAY is the only tracked uppercase label (0.2em). Every other button is sentence case and untracked.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Surfaces separate by tone and a 1 px hairline, never by shadow. A shadow belongs only to what floats over the stage, with its line-strong ring.

rules.name: The One Light Rule
rules.body: PLAY's ember is the only light: the glow under it when lit, the kindle's gold edge, and the stage's ground, which warms with it. Nothing else glows.

rules.name: The Ground Follows PLAY Rule
rules.body: The ground is warm only while PLAY is lit or the game runs, cool while something is being readied or a task holds the stage, and plain ink when Play can't happen. It shows nothing else.

rules.name: The Kindle Rule
rules.body: PLAY's fill is the stage's only ember motion, and it shows only what stands between the player and Play: a check of their files, or the game starting. A download's progress shows on the Game chip and in the Game popover's bar.

rules.name: The One Line, One Action Rule
rules.body: One line says the state; one action, beside PLAY, cures it. No second button, no paragraph: where more is needed, a link opens it (What to try) or a popover holds it (Game).

dos: **Do** keep one ember-600 action in view at most: PLAY when it's lit, otherwise the one primary action of a task, a popover section or a dialog. Under a dialog the 60% scrim sinks PLAY, so the dialog's ember is the one.
**Do** give every state of the stage one line of state and at most one action beside PLAY, its cure: Stop, Cancel, Refresh, Retry, Paste new link, Check for updates, or the Game popover's next step.
**Do** keep PLAY on the stage in every state, closed (ink-800, faint) when Play can't happen, with the reason in the state line or the meta line.
**Do** say what is true in plain words beside every status colour: "Online · 3/10 players", "Maintenance · back around 21:00", "1 file needs repair".

**Do** open Game, Account and Settings as 404 px popovers under their own controls, with the control shown open; keep Add a server, a key and Remove as centred 500 px dialogs, and an update as a corner toast.
**Do** keep the window at 1200 × 720 with minimise and close only.
**Do** ship Cinzel, Geist, Geist Mono and the 焚寂 subset of Noto Serif SC inside the product (OFL); load nothing from a font CDN.
**Do** use the 2 px ember-500 focus ring with a 2 px offset on every focusable element, and keep text at 12.5 px or larger.
**Do** say, wherever Steam or Gameforge comes up, that Fenji never asks for those passwords.
**Do** keep PLAY closed off Linux and say so in one line: "Playing on Windows isn't supported yet."
**Do** name the game only as a fact ("Swords of Legends Online") and draw all art in code.
donts: **Don't** use ember for anything but PLAY, the one primary action, the 焚 seal, the edges of the active seal, of + and of an open account, focus, the caret, selection and progress.
**Don't** bring back tabs, a side column, a blade, key art or a news carousel: the stage holds one server and PLAY.
**Don't** let anything but PLAY glow; no gradient text, glass blur, coloured stripes down the side of a card, popover or note, or hard offset shadows.
**Don't** draw servers as round avatars with presence dots: they're square ink seals over a state bar.
**Don't** use emoji, small labels above headings, or section numbers.
**Don't** use Inter, Roboto or Arial, or any font, logo, screenshot or art from the game.
**Don't** ask for, or offer a field for, a Steam or Gameforge password anywhere in Fenji.
**Don't** add a maximise button or a resizable window.
**Don't** show the game's build numbers or file totals: progress is a percentage.
**Don't** let a status colour carry meaning without words, or put text below 12.5 px.
